callback_unfreeze_stages

Source: R/utilities.R
callback_unfreeze_stages.Rd

Progressively unfreeze previously frozen model stage parameters during training.

Usage

callback_unfreeze_stages(schedule)

Arguments

schedule

A list of named lists, each specifying one unfreeze action. Each entry must contain:

epoch

Single integer. The training epoch after which the listed components are unfrozen.

components

Character vector of submodule names to unfreeze at this epoch.

Value

A luz callback object.

Details

A luz callback that sets requires_grad = TRUE on the parameters of specified model components at defined epoch boundaries, reversing an earlier freeze applied by callback_freeze_stages or by pre-training setup (e.g. freezeEncoder = TRUE). Multiple unfreeze actions at different epochs are supported via the schedule argument.

Component names must match the submodule field names used inside the model. For defineUNet and defineUNet3p the stage names are "e1", "e2", "e3", "e4", "btn", "d1", "d2", "d3", "d4". For defineMobileUNet and defineEfficientUNetB2 there are five encoder stages ("e1" through "e5") and five decoder stages ("d1" through "d5").

Unfreezing takes effect at the end of the specified epoch, so unfrozen components begin receiving gradient updates from the following epoch onward. A message is printed each time a component is unfrozen, reporting the component name and parameter count. The optimizer state for the newly unfrozen parameters is not reset, so any accumulated momentum carries over.

callback_unfreeze_stages and callback_freeze_stages can be used together to implement warm-up schedules where the encoder is initially frozen while the decoder trains, then progressively unfrozen.

Examples

if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
# Train with encoder frozen for 5 epochs, then unfreeze progressively
callback_unfreeze_stages(
  schedule = list(
    list(epoch = 5,  components = c("e4", "e5")),
    list(epoch = 10, components = c("e2", "e3")),
    list(epoch = 15, components = c("e1"))
  )
)
} # }
